title: Conjoint analysis software: how to pick a tool that fits your study
summary: Find out when a survey platform is enough for your conjoint study, and which questions to ask conjoint analysis software vendors before the demo.
body_markdown:
We already have a survey platform with a conjoint feature. Why would we need another tool? +


You might not. If you run standard conjoint analysis surveys on a few product attributes and the results stay within your team, your survey platform is enough. Teams add a specialist tool when their studies need advanced features, and add interviews when they aren’t sure which attributes to test or when stakeholders question the results.


Can you run conjoint analysis in Qualtrics or SurveyMonkey? +


For conjoint analysis, Qualtrics sells conjoint projects as an additional purchase, and Qualtrics conjoint analysis uses a choice-based design. SurveyMonkey conjoint analysis isn’t currently available, but it offers MaxDiff for ranking features.


What is conjoint analysis software used for? +


Conjoint analysis can be effective for both product development and market research and includes applications such as feature prioritization, pricing strategy, and market forecasting. It shows how consumers make trade-offs between features and price, and which combination they prefer. The utility scores can also be used to estimate willingness to pay and how a new product would perform against competing products.


How does conjoint analysis software calculate the value of each feature? +


Many tools use a statistical model called multinomial logit. It looks at which product each participant picked in every choice task, and works out how much each feature level, such as a price point or pack size, raised or lowered the chance of that product being picked. Those estimates are the part-worth utilities. Some tools also use hierarchical Bayes, which gives each participant their own set of scores, so you can compare results between consumer groups.


How much does conjoint analysis software cost? +


Cost varies widely. Some tools have a free tier limited to a small number of respondents, usually between 25 and 50, though most platforms require payment before building a conjoint survey. They sometimes charge per response, starting at around a dollar, or sell annual team plans for a few thousand dollars.


Is conjoint analysis software hard to learn? +


It depends on the tool. Survey platforms with a conjoint question type are quick to set up, because the experimental design is handled for you. Other tools, like those specifically made for full profile conjoint analysis, have a steeper learning curve. They let experienced researchers control the design, for example by setting prohibited pairs so that feature combinations that don’t make sense never appear together.
